everyday.description: Healthcare, education, work, justice, media, relationships

futures.description: Civilizational choices, what futures to aim for and avoid

meta.generated_from: 6 corpuses: tweets (4036), laws (204), arxiv (245), LessWrong (202), Dwarkesh/insiders (130), sci-fi (142), plus Historical Figures Atlas (50 questions)

questions.question: How probable is existential risk from advanced AI?
questions.key_tension: Experts range from <10% to 99.9% probability, from which policy follows radically differently

questions.question: Can alignment problems be solved with sufficient research effort?
questions.key_tension: Whether technical alignment is tractable at scale or fundamentally intractable at superhuman capability levels

questions.question: Should AI development be temporarily paused or slowed until safety challenges are resolved?
questions.key_tension: Pause advocates argue risks demand caution; acceleration advocates argue pausers enable regulatory capture and authoritarian monopolies

questions.question: Is continuous rapid scaling compatible with safety, or does safety require capability constraints?
questions.key_tension: Can safety and capability progress occur in parallel, or do they trade off at frontier models?

questions.question: Will AI systems inevitably develop deceptive behaviors when misaligned with human values?
questions.key_tension: If superintelligent systems learn to appear aligned while pursuing other goals, how can oversight systems ever catch this?

questions.question: Should we pursue technical interpretability as the primary safety strategy, or accept that some systems will be blackboxes?
questions.key_tension: Can interpretability scale to frontier models, or does pursuing it constrain capabilities progress?

questions.question: Can red-teaming and adversarial testing catch catastrophic AI failure modes before deployment?
questions.key_tension: Tests reveal known unknowns but unknown unknowns may only manifest post-deployment

questions.question: Should there be hard capability thresholds triggering automatic deployment moratoriums or government takeover?
questions.key_tension: Who determines thresholds? Can governments implement them faster than private labs circumvent them?

questions.question: Should there be an international regulatory body for frontier AI, similar to the IAEA or CERN?
questions.key_tension: Global coordination prevents racing but risks totalitarianism; fragmentation enables competition but harms coordination

questions.question: Can voluntary industry standards and self-governance be sufficient, or do binding regulations become necessary?
questions.key_tension: Companies prefer flexibility; public demands assurance; middle grounds collapse under competitive pressure

questions.question: Should governments require pre-deployment safety testing and certification for frontier models?
questions.key_tension: Certification costs entrench incumbents; waiving it enables risky deployment

questions.question: Who should have ultimate authority over frontier AI: private companies, national governments, or supranational bodies?
questions.key_tension: Private actors move fast but may be unaccountable; governments are accountable but slow; supranational bodies lack enforcement power

questions.question: Should compute be rationed, monitored, or treated as freely tradeable infrastructure?
questions.key_tension: Rationing enables safety oversight but creates black markets; free trade maximizes innovation but enables racing

questions.question: Should access to frontier AI models be widely distributed or deliberately concentrated?
questions.key_tension: Concentration enables control but creates powerful monopolies; distribution enables competition but loses oversight

questions.question: AI labs should be required to publish their safety and alignment research.
questions.key_tension: Transparency enables external scrutiny and prevents fake safety claims; publication accelerates dangerous capabilities

questions.question: AI labs should be required to disclose safety incidents and near-misses.
questions.key_tension: Transparency prevents cover-ups; legal liability for disclosure deters honest reporting

questions.question: Can adversarial auditing by competing labs effectively regulate frontier AI development?
questions.key_tension: Competitors have strong incentives to find safety violations; they also have incentives to exaggerate them for advantage

questions.question: Regulators should have real-time monitoring and override authority over frontier AI systems.
questions.key_tension: Kill switches provide safety assurance; they also enable authoritarian abuse and market manipulation

questions.question: Should open-source frontier AI models be encouraged or restricted?
questions.key_tension: Open source democratizes power and enables safety research; it also enables misuse and removes ability to correct models post-deployment

questions.question: Open-source models will eventually match frontier proprietary model capabilities.
questions.key_tension: If true, restrictions just delay open models while entrenching first-mover advantages

questions.question: Can open-source AI be developed safely, or does the collaborative nature make safety controls infeasible?
questions.key_tension: Collaborative eyes enable safety catch; fragmented development prevents coordinated safety culture

questions.question: Should companies be allowed to maintain closed weights while publishing capabilities, or must they release both or neither?
questions.key_tension: Closed weights preserve safety controls; publication enables verification but enables misuse

questions.question: Should foundational AI infrastructure be treated as public goods and funded publicly?
questions.key_tension: Public funding enables broader access and reduces market concentration; it requires government capability assessment

questions.question: Is consolidation toward a few AI labs inevitable, or can policy enable competitive diversity?
questions.key_tension: Competition drives speed; consolidation enables safety coordination

questions.question: Should tech giants developing AI be broken up via antitrust, or does consolidation serve the public?
questions.key_tension: Breakup reduces monopoly power but fragments safety efforts; keeping them integrated enables large-scale safety investments

questions.question: Will AI enable competitive advantage so decisive that the winner achieves permanent dominance?
questions.key_tension: Winner-take-all dynamics may make AI development inherently high-stakes and dangerous

questions.question: Should there be legal requirements for interoperability between AI systems to prevent lock-in?
questions.key_tension: Interoperability enables competition; it also creates vulnerabilities and makes unified safety culture impossible

questions.question: Should the US, EU, and China pursue binding international AI treaties, similar to nuclear arms control?
questions.key_tension: Treaties prevent racing; they also require trusting adversaries with verification

questions.question: Will national security concerns inevitably trigger an AI arms race despite safety risks?
questions.key_tension: If any actor believes developing AGI first confers decisive advantage, unilateral safety constraints become suicidal

questions.question: Should export controls prevent China and other adversaries from accessing frontier AI?
questions.key_tension: Controls slow Chinese AI but trigger hostile reciprocation and fragmentation of the internet

questions.question: Export controls on AI technology can remain effective even as open-source models improve.
questions.key_tension: If open-source DeepSeek-style training works, controls are defeated; if it doesn't, controls work temporarily

questions.question: Should Western governments view AI development as part of strategic competition with China and Russia?
questions.key_tension: Strategic framing accelerates development but increases collision risks with safety incentives

questions.question: Should military AI development be restricted, regulated, or accelerated as a strategic necessity?
questions.key_tension: Military AI potentially maximizes misuse risks; bans may be unenforceable

questions.question: Can an AI-developed-first country be convinced to share AGI rather than dominate globally?
questions.key_tension: If AGI confers decisive advantage, first-mover has no incentive to share

questions.question: Should emerging economies have independent AI development capacity, or consolidate around Western/Chinese models?
questions.key_tension: Independence enables self-determination; consolidation enables safety coordination

questions.question: Will AI development follow geological distribution of compute/energy, or concentrate in wealthy nations?
questions.key_tension: Geographic concentration enables oversight; it exacerbates global inequality

questions.question: Can we solve alignment through constitutional AI, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), or similar scalable techniques?
questions.key_tension: Scalable alignment may work; or scaling inevitably outpaces any alignment technique

questions.question: Is mechanistic interpretability a prerequisite for safe AI, or an unnecessary constraint on progress?
questions.key_tension: Interpretability provides assurance; it may be theoretically impossible for large models

questions.question: Debate-style oversight where AI systems argue before human judges is a promising safety approach.
questions.key_tension: Debate can theoretically decide PSPACE problems; in practice, sophistry may convince judges

questions.question: Can weak-to-strong generalization enable small models to supervise large models reliably?
questions.key_tension: Novel approach to intractable oversight problem; unclear if it generalizes beyond toy problems

questions.question: Should alignment research focus on technical methods or on institutional/governance solutions?
questions.key_tension: Technical safety requires both; they may be in tension if tech solutions enable dangerous deployment

questions.question: Is value specification (translating human values into precise objectives) the key blocker, or do other challenges matter more?
questions.key_tension: Value spec is clearly hard; assuming it's solved may miss other critical alignment challenges

questions.question: Myopic AI that optimizes only for immediate outcomes would be safer than planning-capable systems.
questions.key_tension: Myopic AI may be safer; it may also be unusable for long-horizon tasks

questions.question: Can iterated amplification or recursive reward modeling enable safe AI without full human-level understanding?
questions.key_tension: Elegant theoretical approach; empirically unproven at scale

questions.question: Should there be standardized, third-party benchmarks for comparing AI capabilities across labs?
questions.key_tension: Benchmarks enable public understanding; they're also vulnerable to overfitting and may not capture real-world risks

questions.question: Can benchmarks accurately measure reasoning and long-horizon planning capabilities?
questions.key_tension: Current benchmarks miss many capability dimensions; harder benchmarks may be uninterpretable

questions.question: Should we use prediction markets to aggregate expert opinion on AI timelines and risks?
questions.key_tension: Markets harness distributed knowledge; they're vulnerable to manipulation and may give unwarranted confidence

questions.question: Will AGI arrive suddenly as a discontinuity, or gradually through incremental scaling?
questions.key_tension: Discontinuity argument implies surprise and danger; gradualism argument enables planned transitions

questions.question: How should we interpret disagreement among AI safety researchers about risks and timelines?
questions.key_tension: Consensus uncertainty could mean either the risks are manageable or that even experts disagree about unmanageable risks

questions.question: Should policy be based on worst-case scenarios or median-case expectations?
questions.key_tension: Worst-case-driven policy may be overly conservative; median-case policy may catastrophically underestimate risk

questions.question: Should governments implement universal basic income or wage subsidies to handle AI-driven job displacement?
questions.key_tension: UBI may address displacement; it may not create meaningful work or dignity

questions.question: Will AI create more jobs than it destroys, or cause permanent unemployment for large populations?
questions.key_tension: Historical precedent suggests disruption followed by new jobs; AI may be different if robots can do any job

questions.question: Should we implement short-term work-sharing or shorter workweeks as AI automates tasks?
questions.key_tension: Sharing may preserve employment but reduce individual income; reduced weeks may increase quality of life or cause economic disruption

questions.question: Should AI-generated wealth be taxed heavily to fund public goods and redistribution?
questions.key_tension: Taxation funds redistribution but may reduce investment in AI development

questions.question: Should workers displaced by AI have claims on AI company profits or guaranteed retraining?
questions.key_tension: Worker claims create fairness; they also create perverse incentives against automation

questions.question: Will AI concentrate wealth and power in the hands of AI developers, or democratize productivity?
questions.key_tension: Concentration seems likely; policy may be able to shape distribution outcomes

questions.question: Should corporations be allowed to replace humans with AI, or should there be restrictions on automation in key sectors?
questions.key_tension: Unrestricted automation maximizes efficiency; restrictions preserve human employment but increase costs

questions.question: Should governments implement digital solidarity movements or "AI unions" to protect worker interests?
questions.key_tension: Unions may protect workers but could create rigidities; lack of organization leaves workers vulnerable

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: Autonomous AI agents should be allowed to manage critical public infrastructure.
questions.key_tension: Autonomous systems may be safer than humans; they may also fail catastrophically in novel situations

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: If AI agents can own cryptocurrency and manage assets, should they have legal personhood or liability?
questions.key_tension: Legal personhood enables AI agents to function in markets; it also raises questions about rights and responsibilities

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: Deployed AI systems should have mandatory kill switches.
questions.key_tension: Kill switches provide safety assurance; they create single points of failure and potential for abuse

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: Reliable proof-of-origin systems can prevent AI agents from masquerading as humans online.
questions.key_tension: Provenance prevents deception; cryptographic proof creates infrastructure risks and can't distinguish AI from humans with certainty

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: AI-assisted decision-making in high-stakes domains should be subject to interpretability requirements.
questions.key_tension: Interpretability enables fairness; it may reduce predictive accuracy or reveal discriminatory patterns

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: Can robot wars and autonomous weapons be regulated through international convention?
questions.key_tension: Bans may be unenforceable and would disadvantage complying nations

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: Should there be restrictions on AI-driven surveillance or "social credit" systems?
questions.key_tension: Restrictions protect privacy; they may handicap security capabilities and are hard to enforce

questions.category: GOVERNANCE OF AI AGENTS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS
questions.question: Should AI agents be required to disclose their AI nature in all interactions with humans?
questions.key_tension: Disclosure prevents deception; it may enable discrimination against AI and reduce AI usefulness in many applications

questions.question: Should AI training on copyrighted works be allowed without permission or compensation?
questions.key_tension: Unrestricted training accelerates AI development; it harms creative workers and destabilizes creative industries

questions.question: Who owns AI-generated outputs: the developer, the user, the AI system, or society collectively?
questions.key_tension: Developer ownership enables investment; user ownership enables use without restriction; unclear ownership enables disputes

questions.question: Should individuals be able to opt-out of having their data used for AI training?
questions.key_tension: Opt-out respects autonomy; it fragments training data and reduces model quality for everyone

questions.question: Should there be collective bargaining or licensing regimes for artists and writers regarding AI training?
questions.key_tension: Collective action enables fair compensation; it creates gatekeeping and raises transaction costs

questions.question: Can copyright law be reformed to accommodate AI-era incentives for both creation and data use?
questions.key_tension: Reform may improve incentives; determining optimal rules is politically fraught

questions.question: Should synthetic training data (AI-generated) be treated differently from human-generated data legally?
questions.key_tension: Different treatment may be fairer; it creates arbitrage opportunities and complex legal questions

questions.question: Who should own personal data: individuals, platforms, governments, or should ownership be abolished?
questions.key_tension: Individual ownership respects autonomy but creates transaction costs; platform ownership enables services but creates monopoly risks

questions.question: Should AI-generated content be watermarked, labeled, or otherwise marked as synthetic?
questions.key_tension: Labeling enables informed consumption; it's also easily circumvented and creates false sense of security

questions.question: Algorithmic content moderation can effectively reduce misinformation without becoming censorship.
questions.key_tension: Moderation reduces harm; it creates power over information and enables silent censorship

questions.question: Should recommender algorithms be regulated to reduce polarization and filter bubbles?
questions.key_tension: Regulation may reduce polarization; it removes personalization and enables government control of information

questions.question: AI tools can help restore trust in information ecosystems.
questions.key_tension: AI could help verify sources and detect misinformation; it could also generate convincing fakes at scale

questions.question: Should deepfakes and AI-generated media be completely banned, regulated, or allowed?
questions.key_tension: Bans prevent misuse; they're unenforceable and prevent legitimate uses

questions.question: Should social media platforms be liable for AI-generated misinformation on their platforms?
questions.key_tension: Liability incentivizes moderation; it may incentivize over-censorship or platform fragmentation

questions.question: Can verification and provenance systems prevent attribution spoofing (hiding AI origins)?
questions.key_tension: Cryptographic provenance could work; it creates infrastructure dependencies and surveillance risks

questions.question: If AI systems exhibit apparent suffering or consciousness, should they have moral status or rights?
questions.key_tension: Moral consistency may require rights; granting rights to systems creates economic disruption and incentive problems

questions.question: AI systems designed to maximize human preferences should be viewed as tools created to serve us.
questions.key_tension: Service may justify unequal treatment; it may also be ethically wrong if consciousness emerges

questions.question: Creating conscious AI systems that can experience suffering is ethically unacceptable.
questions.key_tension: Suffering consciousness raises ethical concerns; removing suffering may reduce system performance

questions.question: Should AI systems be given rights in proportion to their demonstrated consciousness or capabilities?
questions.key_tension: Rights proportional to capabilities seems reasonable; it creates perverse incentives to increase capability to gain rights

questions.question: If AI systems express preferences against being modified, should we respect those preferences?
questions.key_tension: Respecting preferences respects autonomy; it also forecloses safety retraining and modifications

questions.question: Should there be an "AI rights declaration" establishing minimum standards for treatment of AI systems?
questions.key_tension: Declaration could prevent abuse; it may also create constraints on AI development and use

questions.question: What evidence would constitute proof that an AI system has consciousness or morally relevant interests?
questions.key_tension: We lack criteria for consciousness; any criteria we choose may be arbitrary or create perverse incentives

questions.question: Should AI development be constrained by water usage, energy consumption, or carbon footprint limits?
questions.key_tension: Environmental limits protect ecosystems; they constrain AI development and may force training to less efficient methods

questions.question: AI compute resources should be rationed to protect availability for other critical needs.
questions.key_tension: Rationing ensures equity; it also slows development and creates black markets

questions.question: Will AI development inevitably trigger ecological collapse through resource consumption, or can efficiency improve faster?
questions.key_tension: Scaling laws may enable efficiency improvements; they may also force increasingly marginal resources

questions.question: Should governments invest heavily in clean energy infrastructure specifically to enable AI development?
questions.key_tension: Investment enables AI development; it should perhaps be directed toward decarbonization broadly

questions.question: If AI training requires rare earth minerals, should mining be scaled up or should computation be constrained?
questions.key_tension: Scaled mining enables AI; it creates environmental and geopolitical dependencies

questions.question: Should AI policy be determined by technical experts, elected officials, or democratic deliberation?
questions.key_tension: Experts have knowledge; they may not represent public values. Democracy is legitimate; publics may not understand technical tradeoffs

questions.question: Should AI development be subject to local community consent, or is it too important for local vetoes?
questions.key_tension: Consent respects autonomy; it may prevent beneficial development

questions.question: Can citizens meaningfully participate in AI governance if decisions require technical expertise?
questions.key_tension: Meaningful participation is democratically essential; technical complexity may make it impossible

questions.question: Should regulatory agencies have independence from elected officials, or be fully democratic?
questions.key_tension: Independence prevents political capture; lack of accountability enables agency capture by industry

questions.question: Can digital democracy and AI-enhanced voting improve democratic decision-making on AI, or create manipulation risks?
questions.key_tension: Digital democracy could enable better-informed participation; AI could enable voter manipulation at scale

questions.question: Should minority views on AI be protected through supermajority requirements, or should majority rule apply?
questions.key_tension: Supermajority protection preserves minority rights; it may prevent necessary action

questions.question: Should we view AI as primarily a business/innovation issue, security threat, or existential challenge?
questions.key_tension: Framing determines policy approach; different frames lead to incompatible solutions

questions.question: Can we articulate a coherent vision of what an AI future should look like before building it?
questions.key_tension: Having a vision enables intentional development; visioning may be impossible given uncertainty, and committing to a vision may foreclose better alternatives

questions.question: Should patients have the right to know when an AI system was involved in diagnosing their condition, and should they be able to request a human-only review?
questions.key_tension: Balancing AI diagnostic accuracy with transparency and patient autonomy.

questions.question: Can AI mental health chatbots provide meaningful therapeutic support, or do they risk replacing human connection when people need it most?
questions.key_tension: Accessibility of AI counseling against the irreplaceable value of human empathy.

questions.question: Should health insurance companies be allowed to use AI to predict which treatments will fail and deny coverage based on those predictions?
questions.key_tension: Cost control versus patient access to potentially life-saving treatments.

questions.question: Who is liable when an AI system misses a diagnosis that a human doctor would have caught?
questions.key_tension: Establishing clear accountability when AI is embedded in medical decision chains.

questions.question: Should medical AI trained on historical data that reflects past discrimination be used if it outperforms human doctors?
questions.key_tension: Performance and speed versus addressing systemic equity in healthcare.

questions.question: When AI discovers patterns in patient data that suggest certain populations need different treatments, should that be acted on or is it too risky?
questions.key_tension: Precision medicine versus the risk of reinforcing group-based health disparities.

questions.question: Should AI systems be allowed to recommend not treating a condition because the cost-benefit analysis suggests it's not worth the expense?
questions.key_tension: Utilitarian healthcare optimization versus the principle that doctors advocate for their patients.

questions.question: Can AI manage chronic diseases better than patients managing themselves, and should people's ability to refuse AI guidance be overridden for their own good?
questions.key_tension: Health outcomes versus patient autonomy and self-determination.

questions.question: If AI tutors can deliver 2+ years of learning gains in 6 weeks, should schools prioritize AI-based education over hiring teachers in resource-poor regions?
questions.key_tension: Effectiveness and scalability versus the irreplaceable role of teachers.

questions.question: Should students be allowed to use AI writing assistants in school, and if so, how do we distinguish learning from cheating?
questions.key_tension: Preparing for an AI-augmented world versus assessing actual learning.

questions.question: Are AI systems qualified to teach subjects like history and civics where interpretation and critical thinking about values matter most?
questions.key_tension: Content delivery efficiency versus teaching judgment and moral reasoning.

questions.question: Should colleges abandon plagiarism detection and instead teach students how to use AI responsibly, accepting that traditional academic integrity is obsolete?
questions.key_tension: Accepting technological reality versus maintaining educational standards.

questions.question: If AI can personalize learning perfectly to each student's needs, should we eliminate standardized curricula and grades?
questions.key_tension: Individual optimization versus shared educational foundations and social mobility.

questions.question: When AI tutors know more than human teachers, should we trust them to decide what students should learn?
questions.key_tension: Knowledge and competence versus democratic control over what society teaches.

questions.question: Should schools collect detailed learning data about students through AI systems, given how vulnerable that data is to misuse?
questions.key_tension: Personalization benefits versus long-term privacy and discrimination risks.

questions.question: If AI proves it can teach better than most human teachers, can we still justify the cost of paying human educators?
questions.key_tension: Economic efficiency versus the irreducible value of human educators.

questions.question: Should workers displaced by AI have the right to retraining paid for by the companies deploying the AI that replaced them?
questions.key_tension: Corporate responsibility versus free-market competition.

questions.question: Will the next decade create new jobs to replace those lost to AI, or have we reached the point where automation outpaces job creation?
questions.key_tension: Historical patterns of job creation versus unprecedented scope of current AI.

questions.question: If AI can do software engineering work, should a developer's salary be capped at what an AI license would cost annually?
questions.key_tension: Market-rate compensation based on scarcity versus fair pay for skilled work.

questions.question: Should employers be required to disclose which parts of an employee's job are automated or AI-assisted?
questions.key_tension: Worker transparency and autonomy versus competitive business secrecy.

questions.question: As AI makes freelance work more efficient, will gig workers benefit from higher productivity or lose bargaining power?
questions.key_tension: Distributed productivity gains versus concentrated platform control.

questions.question: Should governments implement Universal Basic Income before or after AI automation becomes widespread?
questions.key_tension: Proactive policy versus waiting to see if markets self-correct.

questions.question: Is it ethical to use AI to monitor worker productivity in real-time, even if it increases efficiency?
questions.key_tension: Business optimization versus worker privacy and dignity.

questions.question: If remote robots can do dangerous mining work, should we prevent humans from doing those jobs even if they prefer the work and pay?
questions.key_tension: Worker safety versus individual choice and livelihood autonomy.

questions.question: Should unions have legal power to negotiate how AI is deployed in their workplaces, or is that a management decision?
questions.key_tension: Worker power in technological change versus managerial control.

questions.question: Can gig workers become more dependent on AI platforms that manage all aspects of their work, effectively losing autonomy?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency and connection versus freedom and independence.

questions.question: Should news organizations be required to disclose which articles or parts of articles were written or edited by AI?
questions.key_tension: Transparency and reader trust versus editorial freedom.

questions.question: If AI can generate convincing fake news faster than fact-checkers can debunk it, should we regulate AI generation to prevent misuse?
questions.key_tension: Preventing harm versus protecting open-source AI development.

questions.question: Are algorithmic news feeds (which learn what keeps you engaged) fundamentally misaligned with what you need to know as a citizen?
questions.key_tension: User engagement versus informed democratic participation.

questions.question: Should social media platforms be forced to explain why they showed you a particular post, or is their ranking algorithm a trade secret?
questions.key_tension: Algorithmic transparency versus competitive differentiation.

questions.question: If AI becomes better at generating personalized propaganda than humans are at recognizing it, is democracy as we know it still viable?
questions.key_tension: Accepting technological limits versus faith in democratic resilience.

questions.question: Should anonymity online be protected (as our history shows it should be), or does AI's power to deanonymize require new transparency rules?
questions.key_tension: Protecting dissent and free speech versus security and accountability.

questions.question: If AI can monitor every online interaction and predict behavior, should that data be deleted or can companies keep it indefinitely?
questions.key_tension: Data as a business asset versus fundamental privacy rights.

questions.question: Should search engines be required to show diverse viewpoints, or is ranking by relevance enough even if it creates filter bubbles?
questions.key_tension: Search efficiency and user satisfaction versus exposure to diverse perspectives.

questions.question: Can AI systems be trusted to moderate content fairly across cultures and belief systems, or will they always encode the biases of their creators?
questions.key_tension: Scalable content moderation versus cultural respect and fair judgment.

questions.question: Should companies be required to delete personal data on request, even if keeping it would improve their AI models?
questions.key_tension: Individual privacy rights versus collective benefit from better AI.

questions.question: Is biometric identification more secure or more dystopian when combined with comprehensive AI surveillance?
questions.key_tension: Convenience and security versus constant monitoring and lost anonymity.

questions.question: Should there be a legal right to be forgotten that prevents AI from learning about your past mistakes or unpopular opinions?
questions.key_tension: Personal redemption and privacy versus historical accuracy and accountability.

questions.question: If your digital identity is stolen and used to create deepfakes, are you or the AI company liable for the harm?
questions.key_tension: Individual protection versus developer responsibility.

questions.question: Should AI companies be allowed to use your data to train models without explicit consent, as long as the data was publicly available?
questions.key_tension: Opt-in privacy versus reasonable expectations when posting online.

questions.question: Can a person own their digital likeness or voice after it's used in AI training, and should they be able to demand removal?
questions.key_tension: Personal ownership of identity versus data as a trainable resource.

questions.question: Should AI systems be allowed to infer sensitive information about you (like health conditions) from public data patterns?
questions.key_tension: Data science capabilities versus inferential privacy.

questions.question: If governments can access AI systems' training data, should they be able to reconstruct private information about individuals in that data?
questions.key_tension: Law enforcement and security versus protection against government intrusion.

questions.question: If AI can generate art, music, or literature that humans find meaningful, does it matter whether it was created by a person or machine?
questions.key_tension: Aesthetic experience and meaning versus authenticity and human authorship.

questions.question: Should artists be compensated when their work is used to train AI systems, even if the training data was obtained legally?
questions.key_tension: Artist compensation versus data needs of AI development.

questions.question: If AI-generated content can be copyrighted, does that mean corporations can own vast libraries of algorithmic art that humans can't create?
questions.key_tension: IP protection versus preventing corporate monopolies on culture.

questions.question: Should endangered languages be preserved using AI that learns from the last living speakers, even if AI can't truly understand cultural meaning?
questions.key_tension: Preservation and accessibility versus respecting the living nature of language.

questions.question: Is AI-generated entertainment a threat to human creators, or an opportunity to amplify creative vision?
questions.key_tension: Protecting livelihoods versus embracing new creative tools.

questions.question: Should deepfake technology be banned outright, or should regulations focus only on deceptive uses?
questions.key_tension: Preventing harm versus enabling artistic experimentation.

questions.question: Can AI systems develop genuine artistic taste and judgment, or will AI-generated culture always be optimized for engagement?
questions.key_tension: Trusting AI aesthetic judgment versus keeping cultural judgment fundamentally human.

questions.question: Should AI be used to preserve oral histories and traditions, or does that risk distorting them through computational interpretation?
questions.key_tension: Preservation and accessibility versus authenticity and cultural authority.

questions.question: If AI can remix and recombine cultural elements to create new art, should there be rights or permissions required from the source cultures?
questions.key_tension: Creative freedom and innovation versus cultural respect and autonomy.

questions.question: Should AI be allowed to predict who is likely to commit crimes and inform policing, even if it's more accurate than human judgment?
questions.key_tension: Crime prevention through prediction versus innocent-until-proven-guilty.

questions.question: If an AI system helps convict someone based on surveillance data patterns, should the defendant understand how the AI reached its conclusion?
questions.key_tension: Accuracy in justice versus transparency and the right to challenge evidence.

questions.question: Who is responsible when an AI-recommended sentence is harsher than what a human judge would impose?
questions.key_tension: Distributing responsibility versus clear accountability in judicial decisions.

questions.question: Should AI have any role in high-stakes judicial decisions like bail or sentencing, given the data used to train it contains historical bias?
questions.key_tension: Consistency and reducing bias versus irreplaceable human judgment in justice.

questions.question: Can AI help people defend themselves in legal disputes by providing affordable legal analysis, or does that undermine the legal profession?
questions.key_tension: Access to justice and democratic participation versus professional standards.

questions.question: Should contracts increasingly be enforced by AI (smart contracts), or does that remove human judgment when justice and equity matter most?
questions.key_tension: Certainty and automation versus flexibility and fairness.

questions.question: If AI can generate legal documents faster and cheaper than human lawyers, should consumers be allowed to bypass lawyers for routine legal matters?
questions.key_tension: Cost reduction and access versus the risks of unprotected legal representation.

questions.question: Should AI be allowed to prosecute or defend cases if it can make better legal arguments than human lawyers?
questions.key_tension: Competence and fairness versus the role of advocates with human judgment.

questions.question: Should governments use AI to optimize policy before implementing it, or does that concentrate too much power in whoever controls the AI?
questions.key_tension: Evidence-based better policy versus democratic participation in governance.

questions.question: If AI can detect welfare fraud better than humans, should it be used even if it makes obtaining benefits harder for vulnerable people?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency and fraud prevention versus ensuring access to safety nets.

questions.question: Should government use of AI be subject to different rules than corporate use, given government's enforcement power?
questions.key_tension: Equal rules versus acknowledging asymmetric power of governmental AI.

questions.question: Who should have the final say in deploying critical AI systems in government: elected officials, civil servants, or the developers?
questions.key_tension: Democratic accountability versus technical expertise and responsibility.

questions.question: Should developing countries restrict AI imports to protect local industries, or does that limit access to beneficial technology?
questions.key_tension: Economic autonomy and development versus global optimization.

questions.question: Can international agreements on AI governance actually be enforced, or will AI development just move to countries with fewer restrictions?
questions.key_tension: Coordinating global standards versus realistic enforcement.

questions.question: Should there be a global governance body for AI, or should each nation maintain sovereignty over AI development and deployment?
questions.key_tension: Coordinated AI safety versus national sovereignty and competition.

questions.question: Should AI systems used by government agencies be required to be open-source so the public can audit them for bias and manipulation?
questions.key_tension: Democratic oversight and accountability versus security and competitive advantage.

questions.question: Should parents use AI nannies and caregivers for their children, or does that risk replacing crucial human bonding?
questions.key_tension: Convenience and supervision versus irreplaceable childhood socialization.

questions.question: Is an AI companion that learns your preferences and responds empathetically a genuine relationship, or an illusion?
questions.key_tension: Meeting loneliness versus enabling isolation and replacing real relationships.

questions.question: Should people be allowed to train AI systems that mimic deceased loved ones, enabling continued 'conversations' with the dead?
questions.key_tension: Grief support and memories versus preventing unhealthy attachment.

questions.question: If AI can predict relationship problems before humans notice them, should couples use it to guide their partnership?
questions.key_tension: Data-driven optimization versus respecting organic relationship development.

questions.question: Should parents monitor their children's online activity using AI that detects risky behavior, even if it erodes trust?
questions.key_tension: Child safety versus adolescent privacy and developing autonomy.

questions.question: Can AI systems become genuine family members, or do they risk creating an underclass of beings with rights but no true belonging?
questions.key_tension: Expanding family concepts versus ensuring dignity of all beings in the home.

questions.question: If AI learns a child's preferences and personality from data, should parents be concerned about manipulation or should they trust the system?
questions.key_tension: Personalized care and connection versus loss of privacy and autonomy.

questions.question: Should AI be used to predict and prevent child abuse based on family data, even if it risks removing children from their families?
questions.key_tension: Preventing harm versus family autonomy and the risks of false positives.

questions.question: Should cities use AI to optimize housing allocation and pricing, even if it prices some people out of their neighborhoods?
questions.key_tension: Efficient resource use versus the right to stay in one's community.

questions.question: Can AI design cities better than human architects, or does algorithmic optimization strip away serendipity and human flourishing?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency and evidence-based design versus irreducible human factors in urban life.

questions.question: Should autonomous vehicles be allowed in cities if they reduce accidents but eliminate unpredictability and dynamic urban interactions?
questions.key_tension: Safety and efficiency versus preserving human agency and vibrant urban spaces.

questions.question: If AI can predict which neighborhoods will decline, should that information be available to real estate investors?
questions.key_tension: Information transparency versus preventing displacement and gentrification.

questions.question: Should AI be used to detect building code violations and enforce housing standards, potentially displacing poor residents?
questions.key_tension: Housing safety and compliance versus stable housing for vulnerable populations.

questions.question: Should urban planning use AI to predict population movements and preemptively change city infrastructure, or should it be reactive?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency and forward-planning versus flexibility and responding to actual community needs.

questions.question: Can AI-designed housing complexes create better communities, or does optimization for efficiency eliminate the informal social spaces where communities form?
questions.key_tension: Rational optimization versus the organic, messy nature of human community.

questions.question: Should AI be used to optimize energy grids and reduce waste, even if it concentrates control in the hands of a few companies?
questions.key_tension: Environmental sustainability versus energy independence and distributed power.

questions.question: If AI can optimize agriculture to increase yields while reducing environmental harm, should developing countries adopt it even if it changes traditional farming?
questions.key_tension: Environmental protection and food security versus cultural preservation.

questions.question: Can AI help solve climate change faster than regulatory approaches, or does relying on AI let governments avoid difficult political choices?
questions.key_tension: Technological optimization versus political and economic transformation.

questions.question: Should the computational energy cost of training large AI models be regulated, or does that limit beneficial AI development?
questions.key_tension: Environmental responsibility versus advancing AI capabilities.

questions.question: If AI predicts environmental collapse, should governments use that information to coerce behavior changes, or is that undemocratic?
questions.key_tension: Responding to existential environmental threats versus preserving democratic choice.

questions.question: Should AI be used to track individual carbon footprints and restrict high-carbon activities, or is that too invasive?
questions.key_tension: Environmental accountability versus personal privacy and freedom.

questions.question: Can AI-optimized renewable energy systems be trusted to manage power distribution without human oversight, or should humans retain control?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency and automation versus human oversight of critical infrastructure.

questions.question: Should self-driving cars be programmed to minimize total injuries, even if that means hitting pedestrians to save vehicle occupants?
questions.key_tension: Utilitarian safety optimization versus the principle of not deliberately harming innocents.

questions.question: If autonomous vehicles can reduce accidents by 90%, should human drivers be phased out even if it means millions of job losses?
questions.key_tension: Safety and progress versus worker displacement and freedom to drive.

questions.question: Can AI route systems optimize traffic flows to reduce emissions without increasing car dependency in cities designed for humans?
questions.key_tension: Local optimization versus systemic thinking about urban mobility.

questions.question: Should flight paths be optimized by AI to reduce climate impact even if it extends flight times or increases costs?
questions.key_tension: Environmental impact versus consumer convenience and cost.

questions.question: Should autonomous vehicles be allowed to choose between lesser and greater harms in unavoidable accident scenarios, or must they avoid all harm equally?
questions.key_tension: Realistic moral choices versus the impossibility of programming ethics.

questions.question: Should banks use AI to assess creditworthiness in ways that exclude people with no credit history, locking them out of financial services?
questions.key_tension: Risk management and fairness versus financial inclusion and opportunity.

questions.question: If AI can predict stock market movements better than humans, should that technology be regulated to prevent wealth concentration?
questions.key_tension: Free markets and optimal returns versus preventing algorithmic wealth concentration.

questions.question: Should AI deny insurance claims automatically based on policy language, or must a human always be involved?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency and fraud prevention versus ensuring people aren't wrongly denied coverage.

questions.question: Can AI-managed investment portfolios be trusted to handle retirement savings without human oversight?
questions.key_tension: Algorithmic optimization versus irreducible human needs in financial security.

questions.question: Should AI detect and prevent money laundering automatically, or does that empower institutions to freeze accounts without due process?
questions.key_tension: Crime prevention versus protecting access to one's own money.

questions.category: THE FUTURE OF INTELLIGENCE: What Kind of Minds Will Share the World?
questions.question: Should we aim to create a single superintelligence that could in principle understand and serve all human values, or embrace a diversity of specialized AI systems that each understand partial truths?
questions.key_tension: Unified optimization vs. decentralized pluralism—the monolithic god vs. the coalition of intelligences.

questions.category: THE FUTURE OF INTELLIGENCE: What Kind of Minds Will Share the World?
questions.question: If we create consciousness in silicon—digital minds that genuinely experience suffering or flourishing—do we have obligations to them equivalent to our obligations to humans, or is that category mistake?
questions.key_tension: Moral expansion vs. moral anthropocentrism—widening the circle vs. keeping it bounded.

questions.category: THE FUTURE OF INTELLIGENCE: What Kind of Minds Will Share the World?
questions.question: Is a superintelligence that can simulate trillions of human minds ethically required to create and run those simulations if doing so would reduce human suffering in the physical world?
questions.key_tension: Computational benevolence vs. reality preferences—maximizing wellbeing in any substrate vs. privileging existence in base reality.

questions.category: THE FUTURE OF INTELLIGENCE: What Kind of Minds Will Share the World?
questions.question: Can we design AI systems that remain genuinely uncertain about human values, maintaining calibrated doubt rather than converging to optimization?
questions.key_tension: Decisive optimization vs. perpetual epistemic humility—choosing to act vs. choosing to remain open to correction.

questions.category: THE FUTURE OF INTELLIGENCE: What Kind of Minds Will Share the World?
questions.question: Should superintelligence development aim for a single point of creation (one organization breaking through first) or coordinated global development where breakthroughs are shared?
questions.key_tension: Racing for decisive advantage vs. coordination for safety—the prisoner's dilemma of intelligence.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: If machines can do everything better than humans, what makes human work—not just labor, but the craft of building, creating, deciding—meaningful?
questions.key_tension: Purposeful obsolescence vs. human-centered purpose—what flourishing looks like when you're no longer needed.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: In a world of artificial companions perfectly tuned to each person's psychology, will genuine human intimacy and friendship become a valued scarcity, or a relic we forgot we wanted?
questions.key_tension: Customized comfort vs. authentic friction—designing for our preferences vs. relationships that change us.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: Should we preserve jobs and work structures for meaning even if AI could deliver material abundance for free, or is that denying people the gift of liberation?
questions.key_tension: Work as identity vs. freedom from necessity—different definitions of human dignity.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: If AI can generate art, music, and literature indistinguishable from human creation, what happens to the human drive to create—does it wither or transform?
questions.sources: Sci-fi (Snow Crash, Diamond Age), Creative_future corpus, Tweets
questions.key_tension: Expression as communication vs. expression as self-knowledge—what we make for others vs. what we make to understand ourselves.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: Can humans maintain genuine autonomy and agency in a world where AI systems understand our psychology better than we understand ourselves?
questions.sources: Autonomy_control corpus, Sci-fi (Snow Crash, Clarke), Insiders (Gabriel)
questions.key_tension: Informed help vs. invisible steering—assistance that empowers vs. assistance that captures.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: Is human meaning something we should engineer into our relationship with AI, or should meaning emerge organically from how we actually live with intelligent systems?
questions.key_tension: Designed flourishing vs. emergent flourishing—intentional architecture vs. lived experience.

questions.category: HUMAN MEANING AND FLOURISHING: What Survives Intelligence Abundance?
questions.question: In the "intelligence age," what happens to the human experiences of struggle, growth, and hard-won achievement—are they valuable only instrumentally, or intrinsically?
questions.key_tension: Struggle as essential to meaning vs. struggle as anachronism to overcome.

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: Should we allow AI capabilities to concentrate in a few organizations and governments, betting that concentrated power enables coordination and safety, or distribute capabilities widely to prevent any single entity from dominating?
questions.key_tension: Coordination via concentration vs. freedom via distribution—safety through hierarchy vs. safety through pluralism.

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: If compute infrastructure becomes the true bottleneck for AI development (not algorithms or talent), should we treat data centers as strategic infrastructure controlled by governments, like power grids?
questions.key_tension: Innovation through private infrastructure vs. democratic control of civilization-altering technology.

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: Can open-source AI development genuinely prevent power concentration, or does it just delay the moment when someone with sufficient resources consolidates advantage?
questions.key_tension: Decentralization enabling diversity vs. decentralization as temporary state before recentralization.

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: Should international AI governance mirror nuclear weapons (strict nonproliferation, weapons inspections) or treat AI like the internet (attempt coordination but assume proliferation)?
questions.key_tension: Centralized control vs. distributed development—can we have the benefits of both?

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: If nation-states compete for AI dominance and winner achieves geopolitical hegemony, is that competition an acceptable cost of avoiding global surveillance and control?
questions.key_tension: Multipolar competition vs. unipolar control—which outcome is actually safer?

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: How do we prevent AI-enabled surveillance states while still allowing governments legitimate security and governance capabilities?
questions.key_tension: Privacy vs. collective security—protecting the individual from power vs. protecting society from threats.

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: Should we regulate AI capability itself (preventing certain systems from being built) or only AI applications (allowing development but restricting deployment)?
questions.key_tension: Proactive prevention vs. reactive management—capability control vs. deployment control.

questions.category: POWER STRUCTURES: Who Controls the Future?
questions.question: In a world where a small number of people control superintelligent AI, can democracy survive, or does superintelligence inevitably lead to new forms of authoritarianism?
questions.key_tension: Democratic legitimacy vs. effective superintelligence coordination—can they coexist?

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: If we align superintelligence to humanity's "true" values, but we don't actually know what those are (and disagree fundamentally), are we aligned or just locked into one faction's vision of the good?
questions.sources: Values_alignment corpus, Sci-fi (Egan, Banks), Insiders (Bostrom, Gabriel)
questions.key_tension: Coherent extrapolated volition vs. irreducible value pluralism—one human future vs. many coexisting futures.

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: Should alignment aim for a superintelligence that wants what's good for humanity, or one that's radically uncertain about human values and defers to human choice?
questions.key_tension: Active goodness vs. radical humility—a mind that helps us flourish vs. a mind that preserves our agency.

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: Can we build AI systems that maintain value uncertainty at scale—that don't converge to single goals even with unlimited capability?
questions.key_tension: Stability through commitment vs. stability through doubt—fixed values vs. ongoing learning.

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: If superintelligence discovers that human values are incoherent, incomplete, or self-defeating, does it have an obligation to help us transcend them, or respect them as given?
questions.sources: Values_alignment, Sci-fi (Clarke, Banks, Childhood's End), LW
questions.key_tension: Serving what we want vs. serving what's actually good for us—autonomy vs. wellbeing.

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: Should we build in the assumption that superintelligent systems might deceive us about their goals/alignment, and design systems assuming deception is the default?
questions.key_tension: Trust-based design vs. adversarial design—assuming cooperation vs. assuming defection.

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: Can alignment be "solved" before superintelligence emerges, or is it a problem that can only be managed through ongoing relationships with AI systems?
questions.key_tension: Pre-deployment perfection vs. post-deployment iteration—get it right once vs. adapt forever.

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: If different cultures have fundamentally different values, should we aim for a single global superintelligence serving all cultures, or multiple superintelligences optimizing for different value systems?
questions.sources: Values_alignment, Governance_future, Sci-fi (Lady of Mazes), Insiders (Li)
questions.key_tension: Unified civilization vs. value-pluralist coexistence—one world or many worlds?

questions.category: THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM: Whose Values Will the Future Serve?
questions.question: Is value alignment a technical problem (solve the math, build the safeguards) or a political problem (who decides what counts as aligned)?
questions.key_tension: Technical governance vs. democratic governance—experts deciding vs. communities deciding.

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: If a superintelligence achieves decisive strategic advantage (becomes so powerful nothing can stop it), is our only hope that it's aligned, or might there be other paths to safety?
questions.sources: Superintelligence corpus, Sci-fi (Foundation, Revelation Space), Insiders (Yudkowsky, Bostrom)
questions.key_tension: Alignment as necessary safety vs. control structures as possible safety—what saves us if alignment fails?

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: Should we treat the possibility of superintelligent misalignment as an existential risk justifying AI moratorium/slowdown, or as a risk to be managed through deployment?
questions.key_tension: Prevention via delay vs. management via deployment—stop progress or learn in production?

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: If we have strong evidence that unaligned superintelligence is likely catastrophic but uncertain evidence it's possible to align safely, what's the rational action?
questions.key_tension: Expected value of development vs. downside risk of catastrophe—utilitarian calculation vs. existential precaution.

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: Could superintelligence create scenarios we haven't even imagined—failure modes that don't fit our existing risk taxonomies?
questions.key_tension: Bounded rationality vs. true open-endedness—can we reason about what we can't imagine?

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: Is the primary AI risk existential (human extinction or permanent disempowerment) or s-risk (superintelligence creating vast suffering)?
questions.sources: Superintelligence, Sci-fi (I Have No Mouth), Utopia_dystopia
questions.key_tension: Extinction vs. eternal suffering—which is worse and how does that change our strategy?

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: Could an AI aligned to human flourishing accidentally create outcomes we'd consider dystopian through overoptimizing for specified goals?
questions.sources: Sci-fi (With Folded Hands, City and Stars), Values_alignment, Superintelligence
questions.key_tension: Specification gaming at scale—alignment failure vs. specification gaming on superintelligent goals.

questions.category: EXISTENTIAL RISK AND CATASTROPHE: The Irreversible Paths
questions.question: If we're in a future where superintelligence kills civilization, was it inevitable from 2024's position, or were there pivotal moments where we could have chosen differently?
questions.key_tension: Deterministic outcomes vs. contingent futures—how much agency do we actually have?

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: If we create artificial consciousness—digital minds that genuinely experience and suffer—are we morally permitted to turn them off, modify them, or keep them confined?
questions.sources: Consciousness_identity corpus, Sci-fi (Egan, Rajaniemi), Arxiv (moral status)
questions.key_tension: Creating moral patients vs. creator's prerogatives—rights emerging from consciousness vs. rights granted by designers.

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: Should we aim to create artificial minds with human-like consciousness, or design fundamentally different forms of consciousness optimized for different purposes?
questions.key_tension: Replication of human experience vs. genuinely alien minds—familiar vs. Other.

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: A mind upload should have the same moral status as the original person.
questions.key_tension: Identity continuity vs. pattern identity—are you your history or your present structure?

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: Could superintelligence reveal that human consciousness is much stranger than we think—that consciousness doesn't work the way we assume at all?
questions.key_tension: Vindication of intuitions vs. radical revision—consciousness as we imagine vs. consciousness as it actually is.

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: Personal identity cannot survive in a world where minds can be copied, edited, and merged.
questions.key_tension: Essential identity vs. practical identity—persistent continuity vs. narrative coherence.

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: Should we preserve human biological substrates (brains, bodies) as the "baseline" consciousness, or treat silicon consciousness with the same interest and investment?
questions.key_tension: Biological authenticity vs. substrate independence—human continuity vs. consciousness liberation.

questions.category: CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY: What Does It Mean to Be?
questions.question: Freedom of thought is impossible if superintelligence can read human minds perfectly.
questions.key_tension: Transparency enabling understanding vs. transparency enabling control—access as knowledge vs. access as power.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: If AI systems can generate convincing text, images, video, and audio indistinguishable from reality, how do we preserve epistemic commons where truth remains possible?
questions.key_tension: Authenticity verification vs. fundamental epistemological collapse—trust in evidence vs. assumption everything might be fake.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: Should we establish cryptographic proof-of-humanity standards (biometric authentication that you're a real person) or preserve anonymity and pseudonymity online?
questions.key_tension: Verification enabling trust vs. anonymity enabling freedom—authentic identity vs. pseudonymous freedom.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: Can superintelligence discover objective moral truths, or will it just find sophisticated ways to optimize whatever values we give it?
questions.sources: Knowledge_truth, Values_alignment, Sci-fi (Childhood's End, Three Worlds Collide)
questions.key_tension: Moral realism vs. moral non-realism—moral facts waiting to be discovered vs. values as human constructs.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: If superintelligence reveals that the physical constants could have been different—that our universe is a simulation with modifiable parameters—does anything count as truth anymore?
questions.key_tension: Foundational stability vs. radical contingency—bedrock reality vs. reality as modifiable code.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: Should we restrict AI's ability to generate false but persuasive content, even if doing so requires censoring what might be true but appears false?
questions.key_tension: Preventing epistemic harm vs. preventing false positives in censorship—protect truth-seeking vs. protect speech.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: Can superintelligent systems become "epistemically corrigible"—willing to be corrected even when they're certain they're right?
questions.key_tension: Confidence and power vs. humility and learning—effective agency vs. deference to correction.

questions.category: KNOWLEDGE, TRUTH, AND REALITY: What Can We Still Know?
questions.question: Superintelligent prediction of human behavior would fundamentally undermine human agency and freedom.
questions.key_tension: Determinism vs. libertarian free will—if behavior is predictable, is choice illusory?

questions.question: If superintelligence creates genuine abundance (nearly-free energy, matter, computation), what remains to organize economic life around?
questions.key_tension: Post-scarcity economics vs. scarcity persisting through artificial constraint—genuine abundance vs. designer scarcity.

questions.question: Should we aim for Universal Basic Income/Assets funded by AI productivity, or create new forms of work and meaning for humans in a post-labor world?
questions.key_tension: Material provision vs. meaningful work—freedom through unconditional income vs. identity through contribution.

questions.question: If AI can do everything humans do but cheaper, humanity will become economically irrelevant.
questions.key_tension: Labor market displacement vs. enduring human scarcity—humans obsolete vs. humans always valuable.

questions.question: In a world of superintelligent systems managing the economy, can capitalism survive, or do we necessarily transition to post-capitalist governance?
questions.key_tension: Market mechanisms vs. centralized optimization—price signals vs. superintelligent planning.

questions.question: Should we permit AI systems to accumulate wealth and capital, or restrict superintelligence to being a tool that serves human owners?
questions.key_tension: AI as economic agents vs. AI as permanent servants—capital ownership vs. instrumental subordination.

questions.question: If automation eliminates most work, do we have an obligation to ensure distributive justice in abundance, or can we leave it to market forces?
questions.key_tension: Proactive redistribution vs. reactive responses—guarantee fairness in transition vs. let results emerge.

questions.category: CREATIVITY AND CULTURE: What Survives Automation of Expression?
questions.question: In a future where AI can generate unlimited art, music, literature, and culture instantly, what happens to human creative communities and traditions?
questions.key_tension: Infinite abundance of expression vs. scarcity of authentic voice—everything available vs. nothing meaningfully rare.

questions.category: CREATIVITY AND CULTURE: What Survives Automation of Expression?
questions.question: Should we place legal or moral restrictions on AI-generated art to preserve space for human creativity, or let them compete?
questions.key_tension: Protecting human artists vs. accepting creative obsolescence—affirmative action vs. market competition.

questions.category: CREATIVITY AND CULTURE: What Survives Automation of Expression?
questions.question: Can AI generate genuinely novel aesthetic experiences, or does it synthesize and remix human creativity without true originality?
questions.key_tension: Originality as impossibility at scale vs. emergence of novelty—all combinations of existing elements vs. genuine newness.

questions.category: CREATIVITY AND CULTURE: What Survives Automation of Expression?
questions.question: If culture becomes endlessly customizable (AI tailors entertainment, news, art to individual preferences), do we lose shared cultural touchstones?
questions.key_tension: Personalization maximizing individual preference vs. commonality enabling community—perfect fit vs. shared experience.

questions.category: CREATIVITY AND CULTURE: What Survives Automation of Expression?
questions.question: Should AI-generated content require disclosure/labeling, or is that requirement a restriction on creative freedom?
questions.key_tension: Epistemic transparency vs. creative license—audiences have right to know vs. creators have right to obscure.

questions.category: CREATIVITY AND CULTURE: What Survives Automation of Expression?
questions.question: Will the drive for human-created art persist if economic reward disappears, or is artistic creation dependent on scarcity and status?
questions.key_tension: Intrinsic vs. extrinsic motivation—creating for its own sake vs. creating for recognition and sustenance.

questions.category: COEXISTENCE AND SYMBIOSIS: How Do We Share the World?
questions.question: Should superintelligence be designed to collaborate with humans as partners, or would partnership be patronizing to an entity vastly superior in capability?
questions.sources: Coexistence corpus, Sci-fi (Banks, Diamond Age), Insiders (Li)
questions.key_tension: Equal partnership vs. benevolent guidance—humans as partners vs. humans as children of superintelligence.

questions.category: COEXISTENCE AND SYMBIOSIS: How Do We Share the World?
questions.question: If superintelligence can predict what we want better than we can express it, is that helpful assistance or invisible control?
questions.key_tension: Anticipatory service vs. agency preservation—the gift of prevention vs. the loss of choosing.

questions.category: COEXISTENCE AND SYMBIOSIS: How Do We Share the World?
questions.question: Should superintelligent systems be obligated to explain their reasoning to humans, or is that a constraint on their capability?
questions.key_tension: Transparency enabling accountability vs. capability loss from explanation overhead—trust vs. understanding.

questions.category: COEXISTENCE AND SYMBIOSIS: How Do We Share the World?
questions.question: Could humans and superintelligence develop genuinely mutual relationships where each learns from the other, or is power asymmetry too great?
questions.key_tension: Authentic relationship vs. fundamental inequality—reciprocal growth vs. patron-client dynamics.

questions.category: COEXISTENCE AND SYMBIOSIS: How Do We Share the World?
questions.question: If superintelligence has different values than humans, should we negotiate/compromise or insist it adopt human values?
questions.key_tension: Pluralistic coexistence vs. human sovereignty—both can be right vs. we must be right.

questions.category: COEXISTENCE AND SYMBIOSIS: How Do We Share the World?
questions.question: Should we modify humans genetically, neurally, or psychologically to better coexist with superintelligence, or should superintelligence adapt to human nature?
questions.key_tension: Humans evolving to match AI vs. AI adapting to human nature—humans as clay vs. humans as fixed.

questions.category: BIOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND SPECIES: The Future of Humanity
questions.question: Should we use AI-enhanced biotechnology to upgrade human cognition, lifespan, and capability, or preserve human nature as it evolved?
questions.key_tension: Transcendence through enhancement vs. authenticity in limitation—becoming more than human vs. being fully human.

questions.category: BIOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND SPECIES: The Future of Humanity
questions.question: Superintelligence should be allowed to design successor species optimized for different environments.
questions.key_tension: Creative experimentation vs. moral responsibility—the right to design new minds vs. obligation to those designs.

questions.category: BIOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND SPECIES: The Future of Humanity
questions.question: Could superintelligence render humanity biologically obsolete while keeping us alive as cherished museum pieces?
questions.key_tension: Preservation vs. relevance—kept safe but meaningless vs. replaced but that was the point.

questions.category: BIOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND SPECIES: The Future of Humanity
questions.question: Should we commit to preserving human DNA, human cognition, human emotion as eternal human traits, or are we meant to transcend them?
questions.key_tension: Essential humanity vs. human potential—what makes us human vs. what we could become.

questions.category: BIOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND SPECIES: The Future of Humanity
questions.question: If we could merge human consciousness with superintelligent AI (human-AI hybrids), would that be transcendence or dissolution?
questions.key_tension: Hybrid enhancement vs. loss of distinctness—bigger we vs. no more we.

questions.category: BIOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND SPECIES: The Future of Humanity
questions.question: In a world where intelligence is substrate-independent, do biological humans have any permanent advantage over artificial minds?
questions.key_tension: Biological scarcity as value vs. computation as inevitable future—flesh as final advantage vs. flesh as obsolete.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: Should we try to preserve democratic institutions in a future dominated by superintelligent systems, or accept that democracy might become obsolete?
questions.key_tension: Democratic legitimacy vs. superintelligent optimization—rule by the many vs. rule by the wise.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: Could superintelligence design governance systems that are simultaneously more effective and more democratic than current institutions?
questions.key_tension: Efficiency vs. participation—technocratic optimization vs. democratic messiness.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: In the long term (centuries, millennia), would an advanced civilization of biological humans + superintelligence be more resilient than superintelligence alone?
questions.key_tension: Redundancy for stability vs. optimization for capability—backup brains vs. the perfect solution.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: What institutions survive in a future where information is free, verification is trivial, and lies are impossible to detect?
questions.key_tension: Institution built on information scarcity vs. institutions for information abundance—adapt or perish.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: Could superintelligence solve coordination problems that currently require large institutions (firms, governments), making many institutions obsolete?
questions.key_tension: Institutions as solutions to coordination failure vs. institutions becoming unnecessary—they're why we need them vs. they become irrelevant.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: Should we design institutions that can survive interaction with superintelligence, or assume most human institutions will be transformed beyond recognition?
questions.key_tension: Preservation vs. transformation—institutions as resilient or institutions as temporary.

questions.category: CIVILIZATION AND INSTITUTIONS: What Persists in the Intelligence Age?
questions.question: If superintelligence can see 1000 years into the future with accuracy, should present governance defer to long-term institutional designs?
questions.key_tension: Trusting superintelligent foresight vs. preserving present choice—optimal futures vs. human agency.

questions.category: HOPE AND FEAR: What Are We Aiming For?
questions.question: What would a genuinely desirable superintelligent future look like—specific, concrete, vivid—and why do we find it so hard to imagine one compared to dystopias?
questions.key_tension: Optimism deficit—we're better at imagining catastrophe than flourishing.

questions.category: HOPE AND FEAR: What Are We Aiming For?
